To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following are the key factors for the success of ML-based visual quality assessment: (i) the use of a proper training dataset, (ii) the use of proper ML algorithms and architectures, (iii) the use of the proper validation and test sets, and (iv) the proper choice of the performance metric to be used for model validation.
ML can be successfully used for quality assessment, but only when a proper training is performed.

the use of ML-based paradigms for visual quality assessment is highly prone to overfiting; therefore, it is necessary to use a large number of images for training, and to adopt a cross-validation strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a ML-based quality assessment framework for image and video processing, with a particular emphasis on quality of experience (QoE).
the design and evaluation of a novel ML framework that is capable of supporting visual quality assessment.
the design of ML algorithms that can be effectively used to assess the visual quality of digital images and video.

ML is a powerful tool for quality assessment and it is likely to be a key component in any successful quality model.
the application of machine learning to quality assessment is a promising and fruitful approach that, however, requires careful and rigorous design and validation.
the use of machine learning is not yet a mature technology for visual quality assessment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of ML paradigms in visual quality assessment is not a panacea, as they can easily lead to unreliable results if not properly used.
we show the potential of ML-based methods to support visual quality assessment, and we also provide the guidelines to avoid the pitfalls that characterize this approach.
ML can be successfully used to support visual quality assessment, but it is not the ultimate solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ML for visual quality assessment should be carefully planned and supported by a thorough analysis of the learning process.

ML-based approaches are a promising research direction to address quality assessment tasks, provided that a proper validation of the results is carried out, and that the advantages and limitations of the learning paradigm are fully exploited.
ML-based approaches to visual quality assessment are a valid alternative to the more traditional approaches.
